started the app without -ea, so assert statements never ran when
developers tried the app from source.

Set enableAssertions explicitly for test and run. Add a test that
fails if the test JVM runs without assertions; it was confirmed to
fail when an init script turns them off. Document -ea for IntelliJ and
for running the JAR during development. End-user java -jar is unchanged.

commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep a copy of an unreadable data file at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file could not be loaded, TutorConnect silently started
with an empty list, and the next data-changing command replaced the
file, permanently losing every valid record.

Copy the unreadable file beside it as NAME.unreadable-STAMP.bak before
any command can run, never overwriting an earlier copy, and show a
warning in the result box that names the copy and explains how to
recover. If the copy fails, the warning says so and asks the user to
back up the file first. Test the copy, the visible warning and that
the copy survives the next save, and update the User Guide caution.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a type-first command bar and light theme
commitResults.messageBody:
The window still used AB3's dark theme and plain label lists, and the
command box offered no help while typing, although TutorConnect is
meant to be driven entirely from the keyboard.

Replace the dark theme with a light TutorConnect theme: a read-only
command reference rail, a header with live counts, list rows with
initials avatars, and a profile panel with sections, beside a restyled
timetable. Add no new mouse-only controls.

Make commands faster to type: Up/Down recall earlier commands, Tab
completes command words, the format of the typed command is shown
below the field and Esc clears it. Typing anywhere returns to the
command bar, Ctrl/Cmd+L focuses it, Ctrl/Cmd+Up/Down move the
selection and Page Up/Down scroll the profile. Narrow windows hide
the rail and counts, and the default window is larger.

No command, message or saved data changes. Profile rows and card
labels keep their existing text, so other features' UI tests still
read them unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add subject command for subject tagging (F06)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds `subject INDEX s/SUBJECT`, which sets one subject per student.
Subjects are normalized (NFKC, trimmed, spaces collapsed), must be 2-50
characters with at least one letter, and may use letters, digits, spaces
and & / - ' ( ). Display case is kept and equality ignores case and
spacing, so a case-only or spacing-only difference is a no-change.
Stored in the shared StudentFields envelope; shown on the student card
and details panel, with tests and user guide documentation.

Also includes the same IndexedParameterParserUtil fix as the F05 branch
(missing-index crash, repeated-parameter message names the prefix).

Story 13 asks for freeform notes on a student, such as "weak in
calculus". Add `note INDEX m/NOTE` to set or replace the single
current note and `clearnote INDEX` to remove it.

The note is stored in the existing StudentFields envelope under the
owned key academicNote, so the student ID and every other field are
kept. A note is 1-500 characters after Unicode normalization; control
characters and line breaks are rejected. The command has one
parameter, so everything after m/ is the note, which lets notes
contain slashes such as "and/or" and "w/". Setting the same note
again is a no-change result and nothing is saved.

The commands hash the index text because Index defines equals but not
hashCode.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assessment record and history types
commitResults.messageBody:
Story 12 needs dated exam and test results per student. An
AssessmentRecord holds a real calendar date, a 1-60 character title
and a 1-20 character grade. The grade is only text, so grading
systems such as A1 and 85/100 are never compared or averaged.

An AssessmentHistory keeps up to 100 records ordered by date, with
records on the same date in the order they were added. The same date
and title (ignoring case and spacing) count as a duplicate. The
history is stored under the owned key assessments as a list of date,
title and grade objects. Decoding is strict, so hand-edited data that
cannot be read is reported rather than silently dropped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assess, assessments and unassess commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Add `assess INDEX d/DATE t/TITLE g/GRADE` to add a record,
`assessments INDEX` to list them and `unassess INDEX i/RECORD` to
remove one, so a wrong entry can be corrected. A record's number is
its position in date order.

The commands keep the student ID and every other field, reject
duplicates and a 101st record, and refuse to touch a stored history
that cannot be read instead of overwriting it. An emptied history is
removed from the file. `assessments` selects the student but never
saves. The commands hash the index text because Index defines equals
but not hashCode.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject extra text after the clear command
commitResults.messageBody:
Typing "clear 1" or "clear all" used to wipe the whole register,
because the clear command ignored whatever followed it. A mistyped
"delete 1" is one word away from that and there is no undo, so the
mistake is destructive.

Clear now behaves like list: any text after the command word is
refused with "Error: Clear does not accept parameters." and nothing
is changed. Plain "clear" with spaces around it still works.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

"find n/Alex" used to search for the keyword "n/Alex", which can
never match because names do not contain a slash. The user saw
"0 student(s) listed!" with no hint that the prefix was the problem,
and "find Alex n/Bob" quietly ignored the second keyword.

A keyword that starts with ASCII letters followed by a slash is now
reported as an unknown parameter, the same message add, edit and the
other commands give. Keywords such as "12/3" are unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Limit the length of emails and tags
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit accepted a 300-character email and a 200-character tag, while
every other text field has an upper bound (name 70, address 200,
subject 50, note 500). Such values are not valid emails under the
usual standard and are too long to show on a student card.

Emails are now limited to 254 characters in total and 64 before the
at sign, and tags to 30 characters. Longer values are refused with a
message that states the limit. Existing shorter values, and stored
data, are unaffected because only typed input is checked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Use TutorConnect wording in clear, exit and edit
commitResults.messageBody:
The exit message said "Address Book", the clear message said
"Address book has been cleared!" and a duplicate edit said "This
student already exists in the address book." These are leftovers
from the original AddressBook project; the product is TutorConnect
and it manages students.

Exit now names TutorConnect, clear says all students were cleared,
and a duplicate edit reuses the wording of a duplicate add, which
also gives it the "Error: " prefix every other failure has. The one
UI test that quoted the clear message is updated to match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Report an omitted index as missing
commitResults.messageBody:
Typing "edit n/Bob" or "rate r/50" answered "Invalid index. Enter a
positive whole number...", which sends the user looking for a typo
that is not there because no index was typed. delete, assessments
and clearnote already said "Missing required parameter: INDEX".

An empty index is now reported with that same message by edit,
guardian, level, subject, rate, note, assess, unassess, payment,
schedule and unschedule. Indexes that are present but malformed
(0, 01, abc, 1.5, ...) keep the "Invalid index" message.
